summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 3.5/63)

data.turoyo: Maḥəsli, ḥatta kəmġašəm b ruḥe w komər: "Lə kuḏəʕ, mən yo." Bas bi xaṣra ḥreto koṯe Qoǧamanoġlu u qaymaqam d Məḏyaḏ ġalabe kayiso l bole.
data.translation: I noticed that he even acts ignorant himself and says, "I do not know who he is." But on the other hand Kocamanoglu, the district governor of Midyat, comes very well to his mind. And he tells how, on Kocamanoglu's order, he was made mukhtar of Kfarze.

rationale: First II.1 Infectum example after round 1. The professed ignorance and immediate recollection make the feigning reading clear from the Turoyo and support the already proposed gloss correction.

data.turoyo: Mġašamle b ruḥe lu kurrəko, omər: "Abre du malko daṭ ṭayre no."
data.translation: Der Junge verstellte sich und antwortete: "Ich bin der Sohn des Königs der Vögel."

rationale: Thin II.1 Preterit cell; overt l-marked boy and b-ruḥe confirm the corrected feigning meaning, with an independently matched translation cut.

after: (mit b-ruḥo) sich dumm/unwissend stellen, sich verstellen
rationale: Both the sole existing Kandar example and PrS 83/40 have deliberate b-ruḥe self-presentation; “dumm, unwissend werden” incorrectly suggests a genuine change of cognitive state. Correct the evidenced meaning without creating another sense or renumbering.

summary: b-ruḥe marks assumed self-presentation with active II, not morphological Detransitive. The subject deliberately answers as if ignorant, concealing knowledge or identity.
The boy in PrS 83/40 is an overt l-marked agent; Kandar’s identity is recoverable from dialogue. These support agency, unlike the inherited change-of-state gloss.
No separate generic “deceive” or cognitive impairment meaning is inferred. The revision is limited to the attested b-ruḥo construction.
kəmġašəm adds the missing II Infectum box to the existing Preterit evidence. b ruḥe remains an overt reflexive phrase in the active II construction, not a Detransitive marker.

The claimed ignorance and subsequent recall give internal Turoyo evidence for deliberate self-presentation. The Jan context independently supports the round-1 sense clarification; no generic cognitive-impairment or deception sense is inferred.

The existing entry already treats this b-ruḥo combination as sense 1, so the construction stays there and is not duplicated as an idiom. Jan has no edition translation; its machine English is withheld.
Is genuine “dumm, unwissend werden” independently attested without b-ruḥo? If so, retain it as a separately supported sense; the supplied material only establishes pretence.
Check Prym–Socin edition references: reader claims prs 141/35, while the actual inherited example has prs 141/37 and prs 241/24. Neither is silently replaced by PrS 50/80 or 83/40.
Provide an approved translation of the selected Jan context; no edition translation is supplied.

Jan corroborates round 1's corrected b-ruḥo sense: the speaker professes not to know who someone is, while the next sentence says the district governor comes readily to mind. This supports feigned ignorance rather than an actual change into ignorance; do not repeat the round-1 gloss change.
